title: Shatter

beats.what: Character wakes in Camden, Maine hospital without ID; disoriented, claims St. Anthony's
Donna reveals the crop is rotten; food shortage hits crisis point after storm
Jim insists on going into the forest to search for Tabitha; Boyd tries to dissuade
Jade found crouched at the wall, repeating he cannot see the symbol; taken back to station
Character at phone borrows a stranger's mobile and calls her mother; brief emotional reunion
Boyd gives Jim instructions on the talisman hut and spider-web markers; Boyd joins
Crops confirmed fully rotten; Victor pulls gun at the goat standoff; Boyd defuses
Boyd delivers rally speech to the crowd: this place will not break us
Jim and Boyd reach strange statues deep in forest; Boyd urges turn back
Creatures drag Tian-Chen; Boyd restrained while she is killed; episode ends on Boyd's devastation

character_beats.beat: wants to hold the community together and project strength; spends the hour denying the depth of his fear while the forest engineers a catastrophic loss designed to break him
wants to find Tabitha at any cost; ignores every survival rule to search the forest, forcing Boyd into escort duty that ultimately costs Tian-Chen her life
wants to decode the symbol and prove he is not losing his mind; is found incapacitated against the wall, unable to see what he desperately needs to see

key_lines.line: It's not your fear that feeds the forest, Boyd. It's hope.
key_lines.why: Previously recap line but frames the season's central antagonist logic

key_lines.line: This place will not break us! The only way we go home is together.
key_lines.why: Boyd's public declaration -- immediately tested and shattered by the episode's closing

key_lines.line: Maybe they aren't panicked enough. Maybe you aren't panicked enough.
key_lines.why: The episode's clearest articulation of the town's denial problem

key_lines.line: I never should have let her go. I'm not gonna just sit around.
key_lines.why: Jim's refusal to accept helplessness -- the impulse that cascades into disaster

key_lines.line: We can't play defense forever, Boyd.
key_lines.why: The argument that convinces Boyd to go into the forest

open_loops: Who is the character waking in Camden, Maine and what did the lighthouse boy mean by 'this is the only way'?
What is Jade trying to see on the wall and why can't he see it?
Why are the trees losing their leaves and the crops rotting -- what environmental deterioration has begun?
What happened to Tian-Chen in the barn and what will it cost Boyd?

contradiction.wants: to project invulnerability and convince his people the place cannot break them
contradiction.does: agrees to walk into the forest to protect Jim's search -- the exact vulnerability the creatures exploit to break him

tone_notes: Density spikes at minutes 20-21 (199 words) and 36 (163) bracket the rally speech and goat standoff -- the hour's loudest social friction. The two long silences (28:35 and 09:15, both ~45 sec) fall around the forest reconnaissance and the recap section respectively, giving the episode a compressed tension-in-town structure before the woods swallow the final act. The episode opens at 125 words/min and never really drops to zero until the closing barn sequence -- sustained dread rather than build-and-release.
